i've got two simple questions !

when i want to "sacrifice" a shambling horde to the Khobar tower, do i gain

Khobar Towers, Al-Khubar [FN]

of the ally.

vamp,
> is the cost of this ally effectively reduced by one for the purpose of

The ally does not remember how it was brought into play or how much was paid
when it was brought into play, similar to Black Cat + Peacy Treaty, as you
stated.

Messages.Author: Nystulc
Messages.Body:
Chris Berger wrote:

>Just out of curiosity, when was the text of Khobar Towers changed? Near as
>I can tell, it just says "cost" on the card, although his post said "[pool]
>cost" so, I guess there was errata... ?

Nearest I can tell, it was never changed.

Apparently, this is simply a ruling. Perhaps it is considered to follow the
precedent of the rulings on Peace Treaty and Kindred Segregation, where
reference to costs of allies or equipment were interpreted as referring to pool
cost only. Perhaps this is now considered to be the default assumption where
there is no specification as to the nature of the "cost" of an card in play.

Is this correct? If so, it would mean that one gets no blood for burning a
Courier with "Orgy of Blood".

outside of the online card text file.

Sorry for the oversight.

>> Is this correct? If so, it would mean that one gets no blood for burning a
>> Courier with "Orgy of Blood".
>
>Vandal counters must contend with blood-costing locations.
>Orgy of Blood will count recruitment cost in blood.
>
>I'll put the Khobar Towers ruling on the RT list.

Then, is there no standard assumption as to the meaning of the term "cost" when
referencing a card in play? If the card fails to specify the nature of the
cost, makes the card ambiguous and can apparently be resolved either way by a
"ruling"?

Or is the default assumption that "cost" includes both blood and pool costs,
and the ruling on Khobar Towers is therefore "errata"?

I'm also wondering how many vandal counters it would take to burn a
hypothetical loquipment location that had both a pool and a blood cost. But
perhaps the design team intends to avoid confusion by never printing such.
